knowledge:
- key_parameters: MAFs=Vector of minor allele frequencies for known susceptibility SNPs ;; betas=Vector of effect sizes (beta coefficients) for known susceptibility SNPs ;; pow=Vector of power of detection for known susceptibility SNPs in the original study ;; span=Smoothing parameter for estimating the effect size distribution (e.g., 0.5) ;; binary.outcome=Logical indicating if the outcome is binary (FALSE for continuous traits) ;; sample.size=Vector of sample sizes for future studies to evaluate ;; signif.lvl=Significance level for future studies (e.g., 10^-7) ;; tgv=Optional total genetic variance (heritability) of the trait; if provided, genetic variance explained is expressed as % of total genetic variance, otherwise as % of total variance of the outcome ;; k=Vector of number of loci to find power for detecting ;; multi.stage.option=Optional list containing al (significance level for stage 1) and pi (proportion of sample size allocated to stage 1) for two-stage designs
- alternatives: None mentioned in the documentation.
- when_to_use: Use this package when you have a set of known susceptibility SNPs from existing GWAS (with their MAFs, betas, and power) and want to estimate the total number of susceptibility loci, their effect size distribution, and the power/expected discoveries of future GWAS with larger sample sizes.
- pitfalls: Omitting the tgv parameter will express the genetic variance explained as a percentage of the total variance of the outcome rather than the total genetic variance (heritability). Ensure that the input vectors (MAFs, betas, pow) are of the same length and correspond to the same set of known susceptibility SNPs.

workflows.name: gwas_future_study_power_estimation
workflows.intent: Estimate the total number of susceptibility loci, effect size distribution, and predict power/discoveries for future GWAS under one-stage or two-stage designs.
input: data.rda (a user-provided data frame or matrix containing columns for SNP ID, Minor Allele Frequency (MAF), Effect Size (Beta), and Power of detection in the original study)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the GWAS discovery data containing MAFs, betas, and power ;; 2. Extract MAFs, betas, and power vectors ;; 3. Run INPower for a one-stage design with total genetic variance (tgv) ;; 4. Run INPower for a one-stage design without tgv ;; 5. Run INPower for a two-stage design by specifying multi.stage.option
workflows.code:
library(INPower)
datafile <- system.file("sampleData", "data.rda", package="INPower")
load(datafile)
MAFs  <- data[, "MAF"]
betas <- data[, "Beta"]
pow   <- data[, "Power"] 
INPower(MAFs, betas, pow, span=0.5, binary.outcome=FALSE, 
        sample.size=seq(25000,125000,by=25000), 
        signif.lvl=10^(-7), tgv=0.8, k=seq(25,125,by=25))
INPower(MAFs, betas, pow, span=0.5, binary.outcome=FALSE, 
        sample.size=seq(25000,125000,by=25000), 
        signif.lvl=10^(-7), k=seq(25,125,by=25))
INPower(MAFs, betas, pow, span=0.5, binary.outcome=FALSE,
        sample.size=seq(25000,125000,by=25000), 
        signif.lvl=10^(-7), multi.stage.option=list(al=5*10^(-5), pi=0.3),
        tgv=0.8 , k=seq(25,125,by=25))
